title: The Safehouse of the DMZ
premise: Felix Coldharbour, a disgraced hostage negotiator haunted by the death of a hostage they failed to save, discovers their voice has been cloned and used to unlock a black-site server run by Meridian, the covert training program that shaped them. Hunted by both Meridian's cleaners and the intelligence service that disavowed them, Felix crosses continents to reach the program's archive before a summit where its stolen leverage will be deployed. In the DMZ safehouse where Felix was once trained, they confront Director Voss—the mentor who built them—and choose exposure over loyalty, broadcasting the archive at the cost of their old identity, and finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Ivo Galloway is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to strangers talk themselves back from ledges before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town whose name they decline to share, on the theory that thrillers are just negotiations with the reader.

chapters.title: The Voice That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Insomniac Felix takes a dead-end corporate negotiation job in Riga and, reviewing a recording of their own voice, hears it say words they never spoke—unlocking an encrypted server ping from Singapore. The beat is dread: the past has learned to imitate them perfectly.

chapters.title: One Failure Still on the Board
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Flashback-tinged chapter: the Marlowe kidnapping, the hostage who died on Felix's watch, the inquiry that ended their career. A former colleague warns them someone is asking questions about 'the Coldharbour protocol.' Emotional beat: guilt weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Meridian Rising
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Following the server trace, Felix finds a defunct NGO shell and, inside it, references to Meridian—a program that trained negotiators as deniable assets. Their own name appears in a personnel file dated years before they remember joining anything. Beat: vertigo of a rewritten past.

chapters.title: The Cleaner Arrives Early
chapters.summary: POV Felix. An assassin hits Felix's hotel minutes after they leave; a dying Meridian archivist slips them a keycard stamped with coordinates inside the Korean DMZ. Beat: paranoia hardening into purpose—they can't go home, so they'll go forward.

chapters.title: Handler Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Nadia Reyes, intelligence officer who once ran Felix informally. She's ordered to classify Felix as hostile but hesitates, suspecting Meridian is using her agency as cover. Beat: divided loyalty; she opens a private channel instead of pulling the trigger.

chapters.title: Seoul, Off the Books
chapters.summary: POV Felix. In Seoul's underbelly Felix buys passage north from a smuggler who recognizes their voiceprint as currency—literally, since Meridian clones sell access. First glimpse of how widely their identity has been stolen. Beat: fury at being made a master key.

chapters.title: The Summit Clock
chapters.summary: POV Voss, Meridian's director. Voss prepares to deploy archived kompromat at a trilateral summit, viewing it as stabilization. We see her genuinely believe she prevents wars. Beat: chilling competence—power convinced of its own benevolence.

chapters.title: Crossing the Line
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The illegal crossing into the DMZ goes wrong; the smuggler is killed, Felix barely escapes into a derelict observation post. Alone, injured, they find fresh supplies—someone expected them. Beat: the trap and the invitation are the same shape.

chapters.title: Safehouse Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix reaches the safehouse—a bunker where Meridian trained its negotiators—and finds their own training recordings, including sessions they have no memory of. Drug-facilitated conditioning. Beat: grief for the self that was manufactured.

chapters.title: Nadia's Deviation
chapters.summary: POV Nadia. She falsifies a report to buy Felix forty-eight hours and flies to Panmunjom under a cultural attaché cover. Her supervisor notices. Beat: she crosses her own line, choosing conscience over career.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Beneath the safehouse: the Meridian archive—voiceprints, leverage files, decades of engineered crises. Felix realizes the summit threat is one node of a living network. Beat: awe curdling into clarity about scale.

chapters.title: What Voss Built
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Interleaved with her arrival at the DMZ compound, we learn Voss inherited Meridian from her own mentor and purified it ruthlessly. Beat: inheritance as corruption—she is what Felix could become if power keeps paying.

chapters.title: Voiceprint Duel
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Meridian locks the archive behind biometric checks; Felix must negotiate with the security AI using their own cloned voice against their real one. They win by doing the one thing the clone can't: hesitate honestly. Beat: reclaiming authorship of self.

chapters.title: The Kill Team
chapters.summary: POV alternating Felix/Nadia. Cleaners breach the safehouse; Nadia arrives mid-assault and the two fight side by side for the first time. Beat: trust forged under fire; the archive drive is copied but the exit is cut off.

chapters.title: Negotiation with the Devil
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Cornered, Felix does what they do best: talks. They stall Voss's strike team by offering a trade—the archive for Nadia's safe passage—while secretly queuing an upload. Beat: the negotiator negotiating for their own soul.

chapters.title: Face to Face
chapters.summary: POV Felix and Voss, split scene. Mentor and product meet in the safehouse classroom where Felix was conditioned. Voss offers Felix succession: the network, the power, the purpose. Beat: temptation rendered sincerely attractive.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix declines—not with heroics but with the truth of Marlowe: Meridian's methods created the failure that broke them. Voss orders the kill anyway. Beat: identity chosen over inheritance; the theme lands.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Felix/Nadia/Voss intercut. The upload begins as the summit convenes; Voss tries to physically destroy the uplink while cleaners close in. Nadia holds the corridor. Beat: climax—all three themes colliding in one room.

chapters.title: Collapse of the Network
chapters.summary: POV multiple brief vignettes. The archive goes public worldwide: governments scramble, Meridian's shells dissolve, assets burn. Voss, exposed, chooses erasure over capture—her ending mirrors the system she served. Beat: consequences arriving everywhere at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath at Panmunjom
chapters.summary: POV Nadia. She testifies behind closed doors, sacrificing her career to legitimize fragments of the leak. Felix, officially still a ghost, watches from the civilian gallery. Beat: quiet cost accounting; some inheritances must be refused publicly.

chapters.title: The Long Sleep
chapters.summary: POV Felix. In a rented room far from anywhere, Felix sleeps eight hours for the first time since Marlowe. They begin recording a new voice memo—one only they will ever hear. Beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Coldharbour, Rebuilt
chapters.summary: POV Felix, epilogue. Months later, Felix trains hostage negotiators openly, teaching hesitation as a skill. A letter arrives with no return address—someone else out there was made like them. Beat: forward-looking hope; the network burned, but the rescued remain.
